question: Where was the headquarters of the National Turmeric Board inaugurated by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nizamabad, Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The headquarters of the **National Turmeric Board** was inaugurated in **June 2025** by Union Home Minister **Amit Shah**.
 
• The headquarters is located in **Nizamabad, Telangana**, a region known for its rich turmeric production and trade.
 
• **Nizamabad** is a prominent hub for turmeric cultivation in India, contributing significantly to India's position as one of the largest producers of turmeric globally.
 
• The establishment of the board aims to promote turmeric cultivation, improve its marketing strategies, and address the concerns of turmeric farmers.
 
• The board will also focus on **research and development**, enhancing the quality of turmeric products, and exploring export opportunities for Indian turmeric in international markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Turmeric in India:**

 
 
• **India** is the largest producer, consumer, and exporter of turmeric globally.
 
• Turmeric is widely grown in states like **Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Karnataka**.
 
• It is known for its various applications in **cooking, medicine, cosmetics, and dyeing**.
 
• Indian turmeric is highly sought after in international markets for its superior quality and **high curcumin content**.
 
 
 
• **Nizamabad Region:**
 
 
• **Nizamabad** is often referred to as the “**Turmeric City**” due to its extensive turmeric production.
 
• The region has a climate and soil type that are conducive to turmeric cultivation.
 
• The **Nizamabad Agricultural Market** is one of the largest turmeric markets in Asia.
 
 
 
• **National Turmeric Board:**
 
 
• The **National Turmeric Board** was established to address the challenges faced by turmeric farmers, such as market fluctuations and lack of proper infrastructure.
 
• It aims to create a centralized system for managing turmeric production, quality control, and export logistics.
 
• It will also facilitate **scientific research** to improve the yield and quality of turmeric crops.
 
 
 
• **Turmeric's Importance:**
 
 
• Turmeric has significant **medicinal properties**, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects.
 
• It is a key ingredient in traditional Indian medicine systems like **Ayurveda** and **Siddha**.
 
• The global demand for turmeric has increased due to its use in health supplements and natural remedies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Turmeric Export:**

 
 
• India exported turmeric worth **USD 236 million** in 2023, with major importers including the USA, UAE, and Bangladesh.
 
• The establishment of the National Turmeric Board will help streamline the export process and improve the global competitiveness of Indian turmeric.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched various schemes to support spice farmers, such as **Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)**.
 
• These initiatives aim to enhance the productivity and profitability of spice cultivation, including turmeric.
